newsitem.title: USA: Bankers Trust adopts new capital guidelines.
newsitem.headline: Bankers Trust adopts new capital guidelines.

text.p: Bankers Trust New York Corp said Wednesday it has adopted the new Federal Reserve and Bank for International Settlements (BIS) capital guidelines incorporating the use of internal models to measure, manage and control market risk.
Bankers Trust said it beleves it is the first bank to adopt the new guidelines.

The Federal Reserve's guidelines reflect new capital standards approved by the Basle Committee of the BIS, which coordinates central bank policies on capital adequacy. The deadline for complying with the guidelines is January 1, 1998, but banks have the option of implementing the changes in 1997 with supervisory approval.

"The Federal Reserve's standards strengthen the world financial system by encouraging sound risk management practices," Frank Newman, chairman and chief executive, said in a statement. "Our leadership in risk management let us implement these significant changes in capital reporting requirements at the earliest possible opportunity."
Clinton Lively, senior managing director and head of global risk management at Bankers Trust, said the new standards more closely reflect the economics of the business.

The Federal Reserve's new guidelines permit banks to measure general market risk using internal risk models. Banks then use these estimates of general market risk in calculating their capital requirements. The new approach to calculating capital requirements will be reflected in the Tier 1 and Total Capital ratios that will be published as part of Bankers Trust's first quarter financial results
Kevin Ferrell, senior managing director and head of Bankers Trust Risk Management Advisory services, said the early adoption "confirms our commitment to remaining a market leader in risk management."
